source.title: Deciphering Two Training Clocks in Grokking via Deep Linear Network Theory with Conditional ReLU Reduction
source.authors: Huihui Tan; Kuo Gai; Shi-Hua Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops a different theoretical and empirical account of delayed generalization through classifier and representation clocks, rather than reproducing the original training recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports modular-addition loss and stable-rank curves, but does not state numerical curve values or report training/test accuracy outcomes. It does not sweep training-set size. The theorem results are conditional on stated assumptions. Cited results about other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper runs its own modular-addition (mod 113) ReLU MLP experiments: train/test loss curves and stable rank across a weight-decay sweep (Figs 1, 3), plus cyclic embedding plots (Fig 2). These bear on V1 and V2 but are figure-only, with no readable values and no accuracy curves. The core contribution is conditional theorems on a deep-linear surrogate. These are a proposed mechanism, not measurements of grokking in a trained system, so they cannot carry verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue delayed generalization arises because classifier fitting (a logarithmic clock) finishes before representation simplification (a polynomial clock). This is proved conditionally for deep linear networks and transferred conditionally to ReLU nets with stabilized gates. The modular-addition figures are presented only as qualitative evidence.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a deep-linear theoretical surrogate and illustrative finite-width ReLU modular-addition experiments; it is not a reproduction of the original empirical recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The empirical sweep varies weight decay over λ ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0}; the theoretical clock rates depend on post-margin gap growth or tail contraction, a sharp late-time KL tail, and, for the ReLU transfer, stabilized activation patterns and controlled downstream norms.

fits_no_version.finding: A conditional theorem shows the classifier clock is logarithmic in 1/ε under post-margin gap growth or tail contraction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under gap-growth or tail-contraction conditions, the training cross-entropy reaches ε in O(log(1/ε)) time.

fits_no_version.finding: A conditional theorem on a deep-linear surrogate: under a sharp late-time KL tail, the structural energy gap closes polynomially, and layerwise weight decay acts as a Schatten-2/L penalty shrinking small singular values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In deep linear networks with layerwise weight decay, representation simplification runs on a polynomial clock, slower than fitting, under stated KL assumptions.

record.problems: The empirical outcomes are presented as figures without numerical curve values or uncertainty estimates. The reported experiments do not provide accuracy trajectories or vary training-set size. The main rate claims rely on explicit conditional assumptions, including a late-time KL geometry assumption; the ReLU transfer additionally assumes gate stabilization.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcomes were left out. The theorem-level fast classifier-clock result is described under fits_no_version because its measure is training loss rather than the accuracy behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No train or test accuracy is reported, so the chance-to-near-perfect transition is not shown in numbers. There is no training-set-size sweep, so the delay-versus-data-size dependence is untested. The train fraction is not stated.
No Fourier circuit is identified and no removal of memorizing components is measured. Whether stable rank anticipates the jump is not shown numerically.
There are no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich intervention.
There is no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
There is no circuit-efficiency comparison, no critical dataset size and no ungrokking. Weight decay is varied only between 0.6 and 1.0, with no reported effect on the delay.
Algorithms are not compared across runs or architectures.
Optimizer and floating-point artifacts are not controlled (AdamW-like betas 0.9/0.98 are used throughout).

missing.what: Figure 2 shows learned token embeddings and output weights with cyclic organization after label reordering. This is qualitative evidence of rule-aligned structure; no row records it.
Training accuracy and test accuracy were recorded during training (per the appendix) but are not reported. The train/test split fraction is not stated.
Optimizer settings: learning rate 1e-3, betas (0.9, 0.98), full batch, 15,000 epochs. These are relevant for comparing setups.

record.verdict_notes: All empirical rows are figure-only and cannot be read, so no verdicts are given. The theorem rows are surrogate-model arguments, not measurements, and are relinked to none. The reader's V2 'supports' label from r16 and its 'limits_scope' label from the stable-rank rows are both dropped. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments do not report training or test accuracy, a chance-to-near-perfect transition, or a training-set-size sweep. The theoretical clocks concern loss and structural gaps, not test accuracy or the effect of shrinking the dataset.

The paper tracks stable rank and structural energy, but does not identify a Fourier/generalizing circuit forming gradually, measure removal of memorizing components, or show that a progress measure anticipates an accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/lazy-to-rich intervention is tested in the paper's own experiments.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiment is reported.

The paper derives conditional spectral shrinkage from weight decay and links low effective dimension to a generalization bound. It does not test whether this produces a more efficient generalizing circuit, nor predict or test a critical dataset size or ungrokking.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

rows.subject: deep linear network (theoretical surrogate)
rows.operation_detail: derived a conditional rate for the representation energy gap

conditions.value: layerwise weight decay represented by a Schatten-type penalty
late-time sharp KL tail with exponent θ in (1/2, 1)

rows.note: This is a conditional theorem about a structural gap, not an empirical identification of a generalizing circuit.
rows.check: This is a conditional theorem on a deep-linear surrogate, with no trained system or measured behaviour. It is not a result on V2's circuit formation. It belongs under fits_no_version, and its 'observed' state is unwarranted.

rows.subject: deep linear network (theoretical surrogate)
rows.operation_detail: derived the end-to-end regularizer induced by layerwise weight decay and the singular-value drift

conditions.value: smooth spectral stratum with positive simple singular values

rows.measure: induced spectral penalty and singular-value drift
rows.value: layerwise decay induces a Schatten-type penalty; ṡi(t) = gi(t) − λp si(t)^(p−1), with smaller positive singular values receiving stronger regularizer shrinkage
rows.note: The result establishes a conditional low-rank/spectral bias, but not a more efficient generalizing circuit or a critical dataset-size prediction.
rows.check: This is a derived identity on weight decay and Schatten penalty plus a singular-value drift formula. It does not measure circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size or ungrokking, so it does not bear on V5.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: deep-linear surrogate under the stated late-time KL and structural-gap assumptions
reader_labels.reason: The conditional theorem gives a polynomial-time representation-gap reduction after fitting; this supports gradual structural progress in that theoretical setting (r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The text describes late stable-rank decrease, but the figures give no setting-specific values and the study does not measure the circuit-level formation or memorization-component removal in the version (r3, r6, r9, r12, r15).
